subject: CAIQ: request to narrow tenant scope and provide proxy artifacts
messages:
From: Emma Foster <emma.foster@northstarhealth.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: NorthStar Security Team <security@northstarhealth.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Aug 2028 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: CAIQ scope question + artifact proxy request

Hi Hannah,

Thanks again for the walkthrough earlier this week. As we prepare our CAIQ intake for NorthStar Health's procurement team, we want to narrow the tenant scope to only the production namespace that will serve PHI-adjacent inference workloads. Our security reviewers are asking for the minimal evidence set and, where full artifact export isn't possible, a way to consume proxy artifacts or sample extracts.

Specifically they asked for:
- A sample of runtime logs demonstrating tenant isolation for a 24-hour window (redacted)
- A mapping of CAIQ controls to Redwood runtime components (the crosswalk) limited to the tenant boundary
- Any guidance on redaction or PII-suppression applied before artifact handoff

Can you confirm whether we can provide proxy artifacts (tarball of synthetic logs + a control crosswalk XLS) and an attestation letter that the samples are representative? We're on a tight timeline — procurement needs the package by Aug 25.

Attached: CAIQ-sample-request-NSH.xlsx (high-level fields they expect).

Thanks,
Emma
Director, Information Security
NorthStar Health
emma.foster@northstarhealth.com
+1 415-555-0199

---

(Attachment: CAIQ-sample-request-NSH.xlsx )

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Foster <emma.foster@northstarhealth.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 18 Aug 2028 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: CAIQ scope question + artifact proxy request

Hi Emma — thanks for the clear ask and the spreadsheet, very helpful.

We can support a narrowed production-only scope and provide proxy artifacts for the CAIQ intake. Proposed plan and deliverables:

1) Scope confirmation
- Redwood will limit artifacts to the production tenant id you provide. We need the exact tenant identifier and date range (24-hr window) by EOD Mon 8/20 to meet your 8/25 procurement deadline.

2) Deliverables (by Aug 24, draft):
- Synthetic runtime log bundle (tar.gz) that exercises tenant isolation patterns and shows request routing and KV cache boundaries.
- CAIQ control crosswalk (XLSX) scoped to the tenant boundary with control owner mapping and evidence notes.
- Redaction guidance PDF that documents fields redacted and the redaction algorithm applied.
- Short attestation letter confirming artifacts are representative and that no production PII was released.

3) Constraints and approach
- For runtime logs we will supply redacted samples (synthetic substitution for payloads, real metadata and timestamps) and an explanation of how logs map to controls. Full raw log dumps are not allowed for production tenants.
- Where a control requires 'proof of execution' (e.g., access logs, key rotation), we will provide hashes and signed manifests along with the sample.

Kimberly — can you confirm owner for runtime log export and propose a minimal redaction strategy? Marissa — will you own the control crosswalk and attestation draft? Priyom — please confirm signing approach for manifests.

If this sounds right, I'll queue a short intake with Security Ops and produce the first draft by 8/24.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Sr. Manager, Compliance Programs
Redwood Inference
hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai

(Attachments: redaction-guidance_v1.pdf)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 18 Aug 2028 15:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: CAIQ scope question + artifact proxy request

Hannah / team —

I can own the runtime log sampling. Quick notes from infra:
- We will produce a 24-hr synthetic bundle derived from production metadata (timestamps, routing headers) and substitute payloads with deterministic placeholders. That tarball will include: request traces, load-balancer headers, cache hit/miss traces, and tenant-identifier linkage events.
- Redaction strategy: deterministic tokenization for any user-provided strings, strip request bodies where necessary, and provide a checksum manifest per file. We can also create a small script that demonstrates the redaction approach so NSH can reproduce locally.

Priyom — can you confirm the expected filename patterns and whether the signed manifest can be PKCS7-signed from our key? We should include a short README in the tarball explaining field mappings to CAIQ controls (e.g., CC-3.2 -> runtime/logs/traces).

I estimate the export + redaction run will take ~8 business hours once we have tenant id + date range. If Emma can confirm by EOD Mon we should comfortably hit the Aug 24 draft date.

Kim
Engineering Lead, Observability
Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.ai

(Attachment: runtime-log-sample.tar.gz stub referenced)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Foster <emma.foster@northstarhealth.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 22 Aug 2028 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: CAIQ scope question + artifact proxy request

Emma —

We've drafted the control crosswalk and a one-page attestation. Deliverables ready as a draft are:
- NSH-CAIQ-crosswalk_v1.xlsx (control-to-component mapping, evidence notes, owner tags)
- attestation_nsh_v1.pdf (statement of representativeness, redaction summary, signatory: Head of Compliance)
- redaction-guidance_v1.pdf (included earlier)
- runtime-sample.tar.gz (synthetic, checksummed, README included)

Before we hand over the sample bundle we need the tenant identifier (production namespace) and the 24-hour date window. Please confirm and we will prepare a DocuSign attestation and upload draft artifacts to the shared Drive link.

If you want the crosswalk to highlight specific high-risk controls for healthcare (e.g., data residency, encryption in transit at session rehydration points), let us know and we will add a short executive summary.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Compliance Program Manager
Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

(Attachments: NSH-CAIQ-crosswalk_v1.xlsx, attestation_nsh_v1.pdf)
